title: Pinned potential dualizing complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, put $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Noetherian means having a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and excellent means having an affine cover by spectra of excellent rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Work on small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a geometric point $\bar x$ write $X_{(\bar x)}$ for the strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point], [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. A geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ is an $X$-map $X_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$. It is immediate if the reduced closure of the image of $\bar y$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$ has Krull dimension one. A dimension function is a function $\delta:|X|\to\mathbf Z$ with $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ for each such immediate geometric specialization, where $y,x$ are the underlying points.

Write $\Lambda_X(1)=\mu_{\ell,X}$ for the sheaf of roots of $z^\ell=1$, with its $\mathbf F_\ell$-module structure. Positive twists are tensor powers, the zeroth twist is $\Lambda_X$, and negative twists are powers of its module dual. Put $M(d)=M\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda_X(d)$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and use cohomological shifts $[a]$.

For a closed immersion $i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with complementary open $j$, $i^!$ denotes the right derived functor on $\Lambda$-module sheaves of $i^{-1}\ker(1\to j_*j^{-1})$, the supported kernel construction [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. For a point $x$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], define $R\Gamma_xK=i_x^!(K|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}})$ in $D^+(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, where $i_x$ is the closed-point inclusion. At $\bar x$ put $R\Gamma_{\bar x}K=(R\Gamma_xK)_{\bar x}$. The strict-local supported-cohomology interpretation is supplied by [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction].

A pinned putative dualizing complex is an object $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ with an isomorphism
$$p_x:R\Gamma_xK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]$$
on the residue-field etale site for every $x\in X$. It is potential if, for every immediate geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$, its geometric-fibre pinnings satisfy the equality in $D^+(\Lambda)$
$$p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}:R\Gamma_{\bar y}K\longrightarrow\Lambda(\delta(y))[2\delta(y)].$$
Here the target of $p_{\bar x}(1)[2]$ is identified with the displayed target using $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ and transport of roots of unity along the specified geometric specialization.

The normalized transition $\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}$ is defined as follows. In $X_{(\bar x)}$ let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$ be the reduced closure of the image of $\bar y$, put $L=i^!(K|_{X_{(\bar x)}})$, and take the normalization $\nu:\widetilde Z\to Z$ [def-sc-normalization]. By [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction], $\widetilde Z$ is a strictly henselian trait and $d=[\kappa(\widetilde z_0):\kappa(z_0)]$ is invertible in $\Lambda$, where $z_0$ is the closed point of $Z$. Set
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}=d^{-1}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Z}(\nu^*L)$$
under that lemma's costalk identifications. Thus the degree is taken after strict localization. The trait transition $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Z}$ is the map of [lem-per-trait-residue-model]: average over wild inertia, use evaluation at a tame generator and inverse evaluation at $1-\sigma$ to map into degree two of
$$M_s\longrightarrow M_{\bar\eta}^S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda[[G]]}(I_G,M_{\bar\eta}^S),$$
and apply this termwise and totalize. The same cited lemma supplies the supported-cohomology comparison and independence of the generator. These are fixed residue transitions; potentiality is the displayed compatibility condition on the pinnings.

split_report.summary: Checked Expose XVII 1.1–1.4 and 2.1.1–2.1.2. Split the definition by its supporting notions and extracted two genuine well-definedness results: the canonical trait residue model and the strict-local curve/costalk reduction. Made geometric fibres and the post-strict-localization residue degree explicit. Reused the existing supported-kernel and derived-supported-sections definitions; no Lean attachment or Mathlib match.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-1c6348db1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, both new nodes, every stmt_dep statement, the base item (the version N3's FIX landed) and its three citers. Source read: ILO Travaux de Gabber XVII, pp. 257-264 (1.1.1 with its footnotes, 1.1.2, 1.2.1.1-1.2.1.2, 1.2.2.1, 1.2.3.1-1.2.3.2 with their proofs, 1.3, 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 2.1.1-2.1.3). Item: the correction to geometric-fibre pinnings p_ybar = p_xbar(1)[2] o sp in D^+(Lambda), with the residue degree taken at the closed points after strict localization, is exactly the diagram of 2.1.2 and the factor of 1.3.1. It fixes the typing only and weakens nothing. The report names the change, and the citers are unaffected (the delta=0 case on Spec k has no instances). lem-per-trait-residue-model is true and matches XVII 1.2. I checked A=Lambda[[G]] =(1-sigma)=> I level by level as products of F_ell(chi)[[T]]. F is exact (pro-p invariants, ell != p), Hom_cont(G,N) = N(-1) is non-equivariant, the constant sheaf gives H^2 = Lambda(-1), a sheaf supported at the closed point gives sp=0, and sp is independent of sigma by 1.2.3.2. lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction is true. Z is strictly henselian local, integral, excellent and 1-dimensional. Its normalization is finite (Nagata), a strictly henselian DVR, and finite, surjective and radicial, hence a universal homeomorphism. The residue degree is a power of p, invertible mod ell. The costalk identifications are i^! commuting with localization and (i i')^! = i'^! i^!, as in the square of 1.4.1. Duplicates checked: lem-exc-henselian-dvr-tame-sequence, lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia, def-sc-normalization, def-pur-etale-supported-kernel, plus DAG greps and a blueprint search; none states either node. Neither node restates a clause of the item. B1-B9 hold. No SGA is cited and there are no tool_uses. No fixes.
